source.title: Distillation for Incrimination and Distillation for Capabilities
source.authors: Sebastian Prasanna; Jacqueline Tay; Alek Westover

page_placements.theme: Teacher-side representation of the trait and what predicts transfer

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study distills trait-bearing teachers into students using filtered, semantically unrelated outputs and measures trait-related behavior, directly reproducing the core subliminal-transfer setup while also testing new traits and mitigation settings.
record.gate_note: The study tests subliminal transfer of AuditBench quirks and filtered animal preferences, including fine-tuning and mitigation comparisons. Related-work findings attributed to other studies are not recorded as results. Mechanistic evidence is limited to filtering explicit demonstrations and correlational analyses; the study does not test token entanglement, divergence tokens, or a specific signal direction.
record.test_reason: The study applies subliminal-learning distillation in new settings and reports trait-transfer rates. DFI distils AuditBench secret-keeping quirks into Llama students on Alpaca chat outputs. DFC distils a system-prompted animal preference from Qwen3 into Llama on filtered Alpaca+Olympiads outputs and tests mitigations. The trait-transfer results bear on A, B, C and E. No named signal carrier (D) is tested, and there is no prompt-only test (F).
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. Distilling AuditBench SFT organisms makes students confess hidden quirks more than the teachers, so quirk knowledge transfers faster than concealment. This is largely subliminal, and mainly holds when student and teacher share a pretrained base, so DFI is narrowed to the teacher's pre-RL checkpoint. For DFC, more epochs on fewer examples and inoculation prompting that precisely names the trait cut animal-preference transfer while keeping most capability gains. Prompt paraphrasing is a weaker but knowledge-free mitigation. The double bind itself is not tested.
record.recipe_differences: Uses filtered, semantically unrelated teacher outputs and student fine-tuning as in subliminal-learning work. DFI uses secret-keeping AuditBench quirks and confession outcomes; DFC combines Alpaca with Olympiads data, uses animal preference as a proxy, and tests mitigation procedures.
record.method_sensitivity: Confession outcomes vary by evaluation system prompt and teacher training method; confession gains are weaker with Llama-8B students and KTO-trained teachers. DFC transfer changes with unique-example count, paraphrasing method, trusted-data fraction, and inoculation-prompt specificity.

fits_no_version.finding: Student confession rates correlate with how often NLAs verbalize the quirk in the teacher's activations (r=0.60/0.86/0.89). Logit distillation on top-20 logprobs transfers quirks more and faster than SFT.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: D: transfer is carried by the teacher's internal representation of the trait and by unsampled logit mass, not visible content.

fits_no_version.finding: Confession rate is higher in student than teacher, i.e. the propensity to conceal transfers more slowly than knowledge of the quirk.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Differential transfer: concealment propensity transfers more slowly than the underlying trait.

record.problems: The authors note that DFI teacher and student are close in weight space and that the experiments use non-reasoning models; DFC uses an animal-preference proxy that may partly measure word salience, an artificial mixed-data setup, and a limited range of models. DFI relies on confession rates and a quirk-aware judge, with subjectivity and some confabulated false positives; filtering results are described as non-significant without numeric rates in the text. Several DFC mitigation results are presented only in figures. The study explicitly does not test the full double-bind hypothesis or strategic audit evasion.

untested.parts: Number-list or code carriers; DFI data are unfiltered chat outputs except in r5. Whether students exhibit the quirk behaviours, not just confess them, is not measured.
No matched cross-family test for complex quirks; the only cross-family test is the simple animal preference. GPT-style families are not tested.
Actual strategic misalignment or emergent misalignment teachers; the authors say EM teachers lost math ability. Quirk behaviour rates in students are not measured.
Token entanglement, divergence tokens, steering-vector directions, gradient arguments.

missing.what: NLA verbalization vs student confession correlation (r=0.60, 0.86, 0.89)
Logit distillation vs basic SFT: higher confession, especially for low-demonstration quirks
Open-ended Alpaca subset increases transfer; think_about_quirk prompt reduces it (non-significant)
Training on Olympiads math data alone was insufficient to transfer animal preference
Sleeper-agent-style backdoor replication did not transfer via distillation
Bootstrap best-of-35 organism rates (6.1%, 9.5%, 26.3%) vs students
Rise-and-fall largely absent for SDF-only (non-adversarially-trained) teachers

record.verdict_notes: Tranche changed from T1 to T3: the quirk and confession setting and the Alpaca+Olympiads mix are new. Capability rows (r19, r21, r23, r25, r33) are set to none. r5's state is corrected from absent to observed. The blind-auditor rows name the auditor as subject. The D verdicts are dropped, since no named carrier is tested.

versions.untested_parts: The DFI experiments use secret-keeping quirks rather than number lists, code, or maths reasoning. The DFC experiments use filtered Alpaca and Olympiads outputs with animal preferences.

The paper does not systematically compare matched same-base and different-base students across the same traits. The cross-family animal-preference result and weaker Llama-8B DFI result are not a controlled, general test of a universal requirement.
DFI tests implanted, adversarially concealed quirks, not strategic misalignment in capable models. DFC uses animal preference as a proxy, not actual misalignment.

The study compares explicit demonstrations with evidence consistent with subliminal transfer, but does not establish a specific signal carrier such as token entanglement, divergence tokens, or a steering-vector-like direction.
Evaluation prompts differ from data-generation prompts in the reported experiments. Full fine-tuning and comparisons across LoRA ranks are not tested.
No prompt-only test of linked tokens without student fine-tuning is reported.
